articles.title: Volunteers Were the Key to NYC-DSA’s Socialist Sweep
articles.author: Ashley Bishop
articles.content_excerpt: Since the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) swept the New York primaries in June, conservative and liberal media alike have tried to make sense of DSA’s meteoric rise by tying them to ascendant New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and his “kingmaking” abilities. Beyond a cursory nod to the army of volunteers knocking doors and making phone calls, far less has been made of the why behind the volunteer effort that propelled these candidates to victory. Across NYC-DSA’s slate of endorsed candidates, roughly 8,500 volunteers showed up to knock more than 750,000 doors, with over 810,000 attempted door knocks — for an off-year electoral cycle. articles.title: HBO’s Burning Man Documentary Omits the Festival’s Workers
articles.author: Keith A. Spencer
articles.content_excerpt: It’s been a precarious decade for Burning Man. The legendary counterculture gathering was canceled two years in a row due to COVID-19 and has yet to recover its record pre-pandemic attendance numbers. In 2023, the indulgent spectacle was marred by sensational headlines about attendees being trapped by torrential downpours that snared vehicles in mud. Moreover, the past decade has seen a parade of negative headlines about Burning Man — including stories of horrific volunteer injuries and a pattern of worker suicides . It’s a weighty moment to release a new documentary series about Burning Man. Directed by Jehane Noujaim and Vikram Gandhi and shot over five years, the four-part docuseries The Man Will Burn dropped its final episode on HBO on July 30. articles.title: Nancy Fraser’s Theory of Capitalism Is Politically Vital
articles.author: Marjan Ivković
articles.content_excerpt: Nancy Fraser’s work has had a significant influence on anti-capitalist politics over the past couple of decades. Some of her insights about the relationship between “redistribution” and “recognition” or the “dangerous liaison” of liberal feminism and anti-racism with neoliberal economic agendas have spread beyond left-wing academic circles and entered the vocabulary of political activism. This is precisely what the tradition of critical theory, in which Fraser situates herself, hopes to achieve, by providing resources for the self-clarification of progressive political struggles. In a broader sense, Fraser has formulated a unique theorization of capitalism that responds innovatively to some of the most pressing questions of anti-capitalist political strategy. articles.title: The People’s Dolly
articles.author: Amber A’Lee Frost
articles.content_excerpt: I cannot easily remember a national treasure that has inspired a larger outpouring of eulogies, memories, and declarations than the passing of Dolly Parton. articles.title: Israel Has Robbed Gaza’s People of Their Homes
articles.author: Mohammed Mourtaja
articles.content_excerpt: One year ago, on August 3, 2025, Israel destroyed my family’s house in El-Tuffah, a neighborhood in Gaza City. Israel did not bomb the house or demolish it with artillery shells. A remote-controlled vehicle packed with explosives drove down our street before detonating. That is how Israel destroyed a house that stood for four generations. During the genocide, our house became shelter for four families. But when it was destroyed, barely any rubble was left. I know how our house appears in the destruction data, because I helped trace and visualize it. At GazaIndex, we trace the data: 134,422 destroyed structures across the Gaza Strip; 34,666 in Gaza City; 2,575 in El-Tuffah. One of them is ours.
